title: Binary provenance ledger and staged CUDA matrix reconciler
creator: Aisha B. Patel
description: Context: We continue to see risk during upgrades where image artifacts are promoted without a reliable mapping to kernel/driver compatibility. Past incidents (see incident 2024-11-gpu-timeout) showed spurious OOMs and failures when a new runtime image landed against an unexpected driver minor version. Goal: build a canonical binary provenance ledger that ties container image digests to SBOM artifacts, pinned CUDA/toolkit versions, NV driver compatibility ranges, and a computed compatibility score. Expose a reconciler that, during rollout planning, suggests safe driver pinsets and cohort assignments and can automatically inject fallbacks when compatibility thresholds fail.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger API accepts image digest and stores associated SBOM URL, CUDA/toolkit version, NV driver test matrix metadata, and generated compatibility score
Ingestion pipeline consumes existing SBOM feeds (Syft/Grype output) and normalizes package -> driver mappings
Reconciler can propose a driver pinset and one-click apply to Dedicated and Private deployment manifests
Rollout controller will block canary progression if compatibility score < 0.75 or observed error rate delta > 0.5%
Console displays per-image provenance, compatibility score and the last verified test matrix (link to CI run)
Automated unit/integration tests and a staged e2e matrix demonstrating at least 3 candidate driver versions
Documentation and runbook added: how to interpret score, manual override steps, and incident escalation path

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from heuristic scoring may block safe upgrades. Mitigation: allow manual override with audit trail and ramp-up threshold settings.
Risk: SBOM ingestion pipeline may miss custom-built artifacts. Mitigation: add a manual ingestion endpoint and require at least one verified CI run before promotion.
Risk: Large SBOM retention costs. Mitigation: compress and tier older SBOMs, store canonical manifests and a retention policy linked to release channels
